key_insight: This paper benchmarks four operator-learning surrogate models for aerodynamic pressure prediction and finds that Bi-Stride Multi-Scale GNN and Transolver(++) are the most promising across challenging airfoil and aircraft cases.
engineering_relevance: The results help identify which AI surrogates can reduce CFD cost for aerodynamics tasks such as shape optimization and load analysis while still handling shocks, large meshes, and limited data.
method: Compare four state-of-the-art operator learning architectures.
Test on 2D airfoils with varying geometric complexity and a 3D aircraft configuration.
Evaluate shock capture, scalability to many mesh points, and performance under data scarcity.
evidence_signal: The benchmark uses two experiments spanning 2D and 3D aerodynamics, explicitly assessing pressure-distribution prediction under discontinuities, mesh scaling, and limited training data.
watch_item: Performance gains may not transfer directly to new geometries or solver settings, so deployment should be validated on the target CFD regime before use.
paper_title: Evaluation of State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Architectures for Aerodynamical Predictions
